{"metadata":{"kernelspec":{"display_name":"Python 3","language":"python","name":"python3"},"language_info":{"name":"python"}},"nbformat_minor":5,"nbformat":4,"cells":[{"id":"15042d98-8603-471c-876f-7c27d3c87e9e","cell_type":"markdown","source":"# 2.9 Hamiltonian Integrity — Validacion matematica en CPU\n\n**Proposito:** validar en CPU (sin fabricar resultados de QPU) el marco teorico que desplaza la narrativa de EQG desde *mejora de AR en MaxCut* hacia *preservacion de la estimacion de observables de Pauli*.\n\nAlineado con el informe EQG Technical Report y el protocolo HIVP.\n\n---\n\n## Motivacion\n\nUn algoritmo variacional no tiene como fin ultimo un bitstring optimo, sino estimar:\n\n$$\\langle H\\rangle = \\langle\\psi|H|\\psi\\rangle$$\n\nSi $H = \\sum_j \\lambda_j |j\\rangle\\langle j|$ en la base computacional (o tras cambio de base de Pauli),\n\n$$\\langle H\\rangle = \\sum_j p_j \\lambda_j,\\qquad p_j = |\\langle j|\\psi\\rangle|^2.$$\n\n**EQG no altera los eigenvalores $\\lambda_j$.** Solo intenta preservar la distribucion $\\{p_j\\}$ frente al ruido fisico.\n\n---\n\n## Definicion\n\n$$\\mathrm{HI} = 1 - \\frac{\\bigl|\\langle H\\rangle_{\\mathrm{ideal}} - \\langle H\\rangle_{\\mathrm{real}}\\bigr|}{\\bigl|\\langle H\\rangle_{\\mathrm{ideal}}\\bigr|}$$\n\n| HI | Interpretacion |\n|----|----------------|\n| 1.00 | Coincidencia perfecta |\n| 0.95 | Desviacion 5% |\n| 0.90 | Desviacion moderada |\n| < 0.80 | Degradacion significativa |\n| < 0.50 | Hamiltoniano pobremente preservado |\n\n**HIS = HI** como metrica principal independiente del problema.\n\n**HRF** $= \\mathrm{HIS}_E / \\mathrm{HIS}_A$ (robustez relativa EQG vs baseline).\n\nEste notebook demuestra propiedades matematicas en CPU. **No reporta HIS de hardware.**\n","metadata":{}},{"id":"2a248f5b-6aa4-4b4d-b283-76cf0db8cca0","cell_type":"code","source":"import numpy as np\nfrom itertools import product\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import List, Tuple, Dict, Optional\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\nnp.random.seed(42)\nOUT = __import__(\"pathlib\").Path(\"hivp_theory\")\nOUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\ndef HI(h_ideal: float, h_real: float, eps: float = 1e-15) -> float:\n    denom = abs(h_ideal)\n    if denom < eps:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return 1.0 - abs(h_ideal - h_real) / denom\n\ndef HRF(his_e: float, his_a: float, eps: float = 1e-15) -> float:\n    if abs(his_a) < eps or np.isnan(his_a) or np.isnan(his_e):\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return his_e / his_a\n\nprint(\"Definiciones HI / HRF cargadas\")\n","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.230392Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.230778Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.239633Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.230747Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.238589Z"}},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","text":"Definiciones HI / HRF cargadas\n","output_type":"stream"}],"execution_count":8},{"id":"91abf6c5-202b-482a-84f9-e25bce407111","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 1. Invarianza de escala relativa: el error relativo, no el absoluto, manda\n3. $\\mathrm{HI}$ cae cuando $\\{p_j\\}$ se aleja de la distribucion ideal\n4. lam))\n\n\ndef depolarize_probs(p: np.ndarray, q: float) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Mezcla hacia uniforme: p' = (1-q) p + q / d.\"\"\"\n    d = len(p)\n    return (1 - q) * p + q / d\n\n\ndef bitflip_noise(p: np.ndarray, n_qubits: int, eps: float) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Ruido clasico de bit-flip independiente por qubit sobre la distribucion.\"\"\"\n    d = 1 << n_qubits\n    out = np.zeros(d)\n    for x, px in enumerate(p):\n        for y in range(d):\n            # probabilidad de mapear x->y con flips independientes\n            diff = x ^ y\n            pr = 1.0\n            for b in range(n_qubits):\n                pr *= (eps if (diff >> b) & 1 else (1 - eps))\n            out[y] += px * pr\n    return out / out.sum()\n\n\nn = 3\nd = 1 << n\n# estado: sesgado hacia |000> y |111>\np_ideal = np.zeros(d)\np_ideal[0] = 0.45\np_ideal[7] = 0.35\np_ideal[1] = 0.10\np_ideal[6] = 0.10\nassert abs(p_ideal.sum() - 1) < 1e-12\n\n# eigenvalores arbitrarios (problema fijo)\nlam = np.array([3.0, -1.0, -1.0, 0.5, 0.5, -1.0, -1.0, 2.0])\n\nh_ideal = expectation(p_ideal, lam)\nprint(\"n=%d  <H>_ideal = %.6f\" % (n, h_ideal))\n\n# Barrido de ruido\nqs = np.linspace(0, 1, 11)\nhis_dep = []\nhis_bf = []\nfor q in qs:\n    p1 = depolarize_probs(p_ideal, q)\n    p2 = bitflip_noise(p_ideal, n, eps=q * 0.5)\n    his_dep.append(HI(h_ideal, expectation(p1, lam)))\n    his_bf.append(HI(h_ideal, expectation(p2, lam)))\n\nprint(\"Depolarizing q=0   HIS=%.4f\" % his_dep[0])\nprint(\"Depolarizing q=0.5 HIS=%.4f\" % his_dep[5])\nprint(\"Depolarizing q=1   HIS=%.4f\" % his_dep[-1])\nassert his_dep[0] > 0.999\nassert his_dep[-1] < his_dep[0]\nprint(\"PASSED: HIS cae cuando {p_j} se degrada; lambdas fijos\")\n","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.267781Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.268108Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.291640Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.268083Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.290818Z"}},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","text":"n=3 Generalizacion: $H = \\sum_k w_k P_k$ (cadenas de Pauli)\n\nCualquier observable hermitiano en $n$ qubits admite:\n\n$$H = \\sum_k w_k P_k,\\qquad P_k \\in \\{I,X,Y,Z\\}^{\\otimes n}.$$\n\n$\\langle H\\rangle = \\sum_k w_k \\langle P_k\\rangle$. El HIS se aplica al escalar $\\langle H\\rangle$ completo,\nindependientemente de si el problema es MaxCut, QUBO, coloring o Pauli aleatorio.\n","metadata":{}},{"id":"334735b2-246c-4469-8046-a19bec84bad8","cell_type":"code","source":"# Pauli helpers (CPU)\nPAULI = {\n    \"I\": np.array([[1, 0], [0, 1]], complex),\n    \"X\": np.array([[0, 1], [1, 0]], complex),\n    \"Y\": np.array([[0, -1j], [1j, 0]], complex),\n    \"Z\": np.array([[1, 0], [0, -1]], complex),\n}\n\ndef kron_n(mats):\n    out = np.array([[1.0]], complex)\n    for m in mats:\n        out = np.kron(out, m)\n    return out\n\ndef pauli_string_matrix(label: str) -> np.ndarray:\n    return kron_n([PAULI[c] for c in label])\n\n@dataclass\nclass PauliH:\n    terms: List[Tuple[str, float]]  # (label, weight)\n\n    def matrix(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        n = len(self.terms[0][0])\n        d = 1 << n\n        M = np.zeros((d, d), complex)\n        for lab, w in self.terms:\n            M += w * pauli_string_matrix(lab)\n        return M\n\n    def exp_statevector(self, psi: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        M = self.matrix()\n        return float(np.real(np.vdot(psi, M @ psi)))\n\n\ndef random_state(n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:\n    a = rng.normal(size=1 << n) + 1j * rng.normal(size=1 << n)\n    a = a / np.linalg.norm(a)\n    return a\n\n\ndef probs_from_psi(psi: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    return np.abs(psi) ** 2\n\n\n# Familias T1-T5 simplificadas en n=3\ndef H_ising_path(n=3) -> PauliH:\n    terms = []\n    for i in range(n - 1):\n        lab = [\"I\"] * n\n        lab[i] = \"Z\"; lab[i + 1] = \"Z\"\n        terms.append((\"\".join(lab), 1.0))\n        terms.append((\"I\" * n, -0.5))  # offset opcional\n    return PauliH(terms)\n\ndef H_random(n=3, n_terms=6, seed=0) -> PauliH:\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    terms = []\n    for _ in range(n_terms):\n        lab = \"\".join(rng.choice(list(\"IXYZ\")) for _ in range(n))\n        terms.append((lab, float(rng.normal())))\n    return PauliH(terms)\n\nfamilies = {\n    \"T1_IsingPath\": H_ising_path(3),\n    \"T5_RandomPauli\": H_random(3, seed=7),\n}\n\nrng = np.random.default_rng(0)\npsi = random_state(3, rng)\nprint(\"|psi|^2 sum =\", probs_from_psi(psi).sum())\n\nfor name, H in families.items():\n    h_id = H.exp_statevector(psi)\n    # ruido: mezclar estado con maximamente mezclado (depolarizing de estado)\n    p_mix = 0.3\n    rho_diag = (1 - p_mix) * probs_from_psi(psi) + p_mix / 8\n    # aproximacion: solo usamos poblaciones (fase destruida) -> cota pesimista tipo decoherencia\n    # Para <H> exacto bajo depolarizing completo de estado:\n    # rho = (1-p)|psi><psi| + p I/d  => <H> = (1-p)<H>_psi + p Tr(H)/d\n    M = H.matrix()\n    trH_d = float(np.real(np.trace(M))) / 8\n    h_re = (1 - p_mix) * h_id + p_mix * trH_d\n    his = HI(h_id, h_re)\n    print(\"%s  <H>_id=%.4f  <H>_re=%.4f  HIS=%.4f\" % (name, h_id, h_re, his))\n    assert 0 <= his <= 1 or his < 0  # puede ser <0 si real se aleja mucho\nprint(\"PASSED: HIS aplicable a Ising y Pauli aleatorio con el mismo formula\")\n","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.910885Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.911559Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.934387Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.911532Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-10-12T14:19:53.933625Z"}},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","text":"|psi|^2 sum = 1.0\nT1_IsingPath  <H>_id=-0.8567  <H>_re=-0.8997  HIS=0.9498\nT5_RandomPauli  <H>_id=-0.4431  <H>_re=-0.3102  HIS=0.7000\nPASSED: HIS aplicable a Ising y Pauli aleatorio con el mismo formula\n","output_type":"stream"}],"execution_count":12},{"id":"b774d6d9-6a76-491c-bcaf-77837dfc0d2c","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 4. Alcance cientifico reformulado\n\n| Antes | Ahora |\n|-------|-------|\n| EQG mejora QAOA MaxCut | EQG es una capa autonoma de **preservacion de observables** formulados como Hamiltonianos de Pauli |\n| Metrica central: AR | Metrica central transversal: **HIS** (AR sigue siendo complementaria donde aplique) |\n| Problema unico N=8 p=2 | Ising, QUBO, portfolio, coloring, scheduling, Pauli aleatorio |\n\n### Problemas compatibles (sin cambio conceptual)\n\n- Optimizacion Ising / QUBO  \n- Portfolio optimization (mapeo QUBO)  \n- Graph coloring, routing, scheduling (mapeo Ising/QUBO)  \n- Cualquier $H = \\sum_k w_k P_k$\n\n### Lo que este notebook demuestra vs no demuestra\n\n| Demuestra (CPU) | No demuestra |\n|-----------------|--------------|\n| HI bien definido y con propiedades de sanidad | HIS medido en ibm_fez / marrakesh / kingston |\n| HIS responde a degradacion de $\\{p_j\\}$ con $\\lambda_j$ fijos | Que EQG en hardware eleva HIS (eso es HIVP en QPU) |\n| Misma formula para Ising y Pauli aleatorio | Optimalidad de umbrales de Judgment |\n| Contrastes H1–H4 tienen sentido matematico | Signo experimental de esos contrastes en HIS |\n","metadata":{}},{"id":"94fd0f13-92ae-45fe-ab73-2aaccc9acc53","cell_type":"code","source":"# Resumen ejecutable para el informe\nsummary = {\n    \"section\": \"2.9 Hamiltonian Integrity Theory and Generalization Beyond MaxCut\",\n    \"metric\": \"HI = 1 -
